title: 08. Files & Errors: 15. os, sys, subprocess, pathlib, shutil & friends
summary: The standard-library toolkit for filesystems, processes, and the runtime environment.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: > The standard-library toolkit for filesystems, processes, and the runtime environment.

sections.title: 1. os — Operating System Interface
sections.body:
### 1.1 Working directory & paths

```python
import os
os.getcwd()                    # current working dir
os.chdir("/tmp")               # change cwd (process-wide!)
os.listdir(".")                # filenames in dir (no recursion)
os.scandir(".")                # iterator of DirEntry — faster, has stat cached
```

### 1.2 `os.walk` — recursive traversal

```python
for root, dirs, files in os.walk("/var/log"):
    for f in files:
        full = os.path.join(root, f)
    dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if not d.startswith(".")]   # prune
```

Mutating `dirs` in place controls descent.

### 1.3 `os.path` (legacy; prefer `pathlib`)

| Function                              | Purpose                     |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `join(a, b)`                          | OS-correct separator        |
| `split(p)`                            | (head, tail)                |
| `splitext(p)`                         | (root, ext)                 |
| `basename(p)` / `dirname(p)`          |                             |
| `abspath(p)` / `realpath(p)`          | absolute / resolve symlinks |
| `exists`, `isfile`, `isdir`, `islink` | predicates                  |
| `getsize`, `getmtime`, `getatime`     | metadata                    |
| `expanduser("~/x")`                   | expand `~`                  |
| `expandvars("$HOME/x")`               | expand env vars             |

### 1.4 File ops

```python
os.rename(src, dst)            # atomic on same filesystem
os.replace(src, dst)           # like rename but always overwrites cross-platform
os.remove(path) / os.unlink    # delete file
os.mkdir(p)         os.makedirs(p, exist_ok=True)
os.rmdir(p)                    # only empty dirs (use shutil.rmtree for recursive)
os.symlink(target, link)
os.chmod(p, 0o644)
os.stat(p)                     # st_size, st_mtime, st_mode, st_ino, ...
os.access(p, os.R_OK)          # permission check (TOCTOU-prone — avoid)
```

### 1.5 Environment variables

```python
os.environ["HOME"]                    # KeyError if missing
os.environ.get("API_KEY", "default")
os.getenv("X", "default")             # equivalent
os.environ["NEW"] = "value"           # set for child processes
del os.environ["NEW"]
```

Changes affect only this process and its children, not the parent shell.

### 1.6 Process control

```python
os.getpid()                  # this process
os.getppid()                 # parent
os.cpu_count()               # logical CPUs
os.fork()                    # POSIX only; multiprocessing is preferred
os._exit(0)                  # immediate exit, no cleanup (use in child after fork)
```

sections.title: 2. sys — Interpreter Hooks
sections.body:
```python
import sys
sys.argv                  # ['script.py', 'arg1', 'arg2']
sys.executable            # path to current Python interpreter
sys.version, sys.version_info
sys.platform              # 'linux', 'darwin', 'win32'
sys.path                  # module search path (list — mutable)
sys.modules               # dict of imported modules
sys.stdin / stdout / stderr   # text streams
sys.exit(1)               # raises SystemExit(1)
sys.maxsize               # platform max int for sizes
sys.getsizeof(obj)        # bytes for that object
sys.setrecursionlimit(2000)
sys.exc_info()            # (type, value, traceback) of current exception
sys.intern("s")           # force string interning
```

### Standard streams as binary

```python
sys.stdout.buffer.write(b"\x00\x01")   # bypass text encoding
```

sections.title: 3. pathlib — Object-Oriented Paths (preferred over os.path)
sections.body:
```python
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("/var/log/syslog")
p.name              # 'syslog'
p.stem              # 'syslog'
p.suffix            # ''
p.parent            # Path('/var/log')
p.parts             # ('/', 'var', 'log', 'syslog')
p.exists() / .is_file() / .is_dir() / .is_symlink()
p.stat().st_size
p.with_suffix(".bak")
p.with_name("other.log")
Path.home()             # ~
Path.cwd()              # cwd
```

### Joining

```python
Path("/var") / "log" / "app.log"
```

### Reading / writing

```python
p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
p.write_text("hello", encoding="utf-8")
p.read_bytes(); p.write_bytes(b"...")
with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f: ...
```

### Directory ops

```python
p.iterdir()                    # immediate children
p.glob("*.log")                # current dir
p.rglob("*.log")               # recursive
p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
p.rmdir()                      # empty dir only
p.unlink(missing_ok=True)      # delete file
```

### Resolving

```python
Path("../x").resolve()         # absolute, follow symlinks
p.absolute()                   # absolute, no symlink resolution
p.relative_to("/var")          # relative path or ValueError
```

sections.title: 4. shutil — High-Level File Ops
sections.body:
```python
import shutil
shutil.copy(src, dst)              # copy file (metadata partial)
shutil.copy2(src, dst)             # also preserve mtime/permissions
shutil.copyfile(src, dst)          # contents only
shutil.copytree(src, dst, dirs_exist_ok=True)
shutil.move(src, dst)              # rename or copy+delete cross-fs
shutil.rmtree(p, ignore_errors=False)
shutil.disk_usage("/")             # (total, used, free)
shutil.which("python3")            # path or None — like `which`
shutil.make_archive("backup", "zip", "/data")
shutil.unpack_archive("backup.zip", "/restore")
shutil.chown(p, user="alice", group="staff")
```

`copytree` errors if dst exists unless `dirs_exist_ok=True` (3.8+).

sections.title: 5. tempfile — Safe Temp Files
sections.body:
```python
import tempfile

with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", delete=False) as f:
    f.write("data")
    path = f.name
# Use path; clean up manually because delete=False

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    # auto-deleted on context exit
    ...

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".log")    # low-level
tempfile.gettempdir()                          # /tmp or %TEMP%
```

`NamedTemporaryFile` on Windows can't be reopened while open — set `delete=False` and clean up yourself.

sections.title: 6. subprocess — Run External Commands
sections.body:
### 6.1 `run` (preferred, since 3.5)

```python
import subprocess
r = subprocess.run(
    ["ls", "-l", "/tmp"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,            # decode stdout/stderr as str
    check=True,           # raise CalledProcessError on non-zero exit
    timeout=10,
    env={**os.environ, "TZ": "UTC"},
    cwd="/var",
)
r.stdout, r.stderr, r.returncode
```

### 6.2 Argument list vs `shell=True`

**Always pass a list** unless you specifically need a shell.

```python
# ✅ safe
subprocess.run(["grep", pattern, file])

# ❌ shell injection risk if `pattern` is user input
subprocess.run(f"grep {pattern} {file}", shell=True)
```

If you must use `shell=True`, sanitize with `shlex.quote`:

```python
import shlex
cmd = f"grep {shlex.quote(pattern)} {shlex.quote(file)}"
subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True)
```

### 6.3 Streaming with `Popen`

```python
proc = subprocess.Popen(
    ["tail", "-f", "/var/log/x"],
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True,
)
try:
    for line in proc.stdout:
        print(line, end="")
finally:
    proc.terminate(); proc.wait(timeout=5)
```

### 6.4 Pipelines

```python
# ps aux | grep python
p1 = subprocess.Popen(["ps", "aux"], stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
p2 = subprocess.Popen(["grep", "python"], stdin=p1.stdout, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
p1.stdout.close()      # let p1 receive SIGPIPE if p2 exits
out, _ = p2.communicate()
```

### 6.5 Common pitfalls

| Pitfall                                     | Why                      | Fix                                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| Reading `proc.stdout` while writing `stdin` | deadlock if buffers fill | use `communicate()` or `asyncio`          |
| Forgetting `text=True`                      | bytes vs str confusion   | always set `text=True` for textual output |
| `shell=True` with f-strings                 | injection                | `shlex.quote` or list args                |
| Ignoring exit code                          | silent failures          | `check=True` or check `returncode`        |
| No `timeout`                                | hangs forever            | always set timeout for external commands  |

sections.title: 7. glob — Shell-Style Wildcards
sections.body:
```python
import glob
glob.glob("*.py")                 # current dir
glob.glob("**/*.py", recursive=True)
glob.iglob(pattern)               # iterator version
glob.escape("file[1].txt")        # escape special chars
```

Equivalent in `pathlib`:

```python
list(Path(".").rglob("*.py"))
```

sections.title: 8. argparse — CLI Parsing
sections.body:
```python
import argparse
p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="My tool")
p.add_argument("path")                                  # positional
p.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")  # flag
p.add_argument("-n", "--count", type=int, default=1)
p.add_argument("--mode", choices=["fast", "safe"])
p.add_argument("files", nargs="+")                      # 1 or more
args = p.parse_args()
print(args.path, args.verbose, args.count)
```

Sub-commands:

```python
sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
add_p = sub.add_parser("add"); add_p.add_argument("item")
del_p = sub.add_parser("del"); del_p.add_argument("item")
```

For richer CLIs: `click`, `typer`.

sections.title: 9. platform and getpass
sections.body:
```python
import platform
platform.system()        # 'Linux', 'Darwin', 'Windows'
platform.release()
platform.machine()       # 'x86_64', 'arm64'
platform.python_version()

import getpass
getpass.getuser()        # current user name
pw = getpass.getpass("Password: ")  # no echo
```

sections.title: 10. signal — Signal Handlers (POSIX-focused)
sections.body:
```python
import signal, sys

def graceful(signum, frame):
    print("shutting down")
    sys.exit(0)

signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, graceful)
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, graceful)
```

Notes:

- Only the **main thread** can install handlers.
- Handlers run between bytecode instructions — keep them tiny; defer work via flag/`Event`.
- Windows supports a small subset (SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGBREAK).
- For async apps use `loop.add_signal_handler` (POSIX only).

sections.title: 11. logging Quick Recap (deep dive in 18)
sections.body:
```python
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO,
                    format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
log.info("started")
log.exception("failed")     # includes traceback if inside except
```

Prefer `logging` over `print` in any non-trivial program.

sections.title: 12. Cross-Platform Tips
sections.body:
| Need              | Cross-platform answer                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Path separator    | `os.sep`, or use `pathlib`                 |
| Line ending       | open in text mode; or `newline=""` for csv |
| Home dir          | `Path.home()`                              |
| Temp dir          | `tempfile.gettempdir()`                    |
| Executable lookup | `shutil.which(name)`                       |
| Atomic file write | write to temp, then `os.replace`           |
| Detect OS         | `sys.platform.startswith("win")`           |

### Atomic write recipe

```python
def atomic_write(path: Path, data: str):
    tmp = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(data, encoding="utf-8")
    os.replace(tmp, path)        # atomic on same filesystem
```
